new_statements.quote: Los radicales simples de la lengua mazahua tienen un patrón trocaico silábico, es decir, una sílaba fuerte y otra sílaba débil (Knapp 2008: 95, Arellanes y Romero 2022: 2). [...] Lo primero a considerar es que la lengua es bisilábica del tipo (2b), y siempre busca reflejar esa posibilidad en sus niveles (fonética, morfológica y sintáctica). Segundo, el acento y el tono distintivo caen en la primera sílaba del radical simple (o compuesto), el tono de la segunda sílaba del radical (o formativo temático) es totalmente predecible, véase la Tabla 4 abajo. En esta línea, los lexemas monosilábicos del tipo (2a) [...] presentan un proceso de rearticulación fonético cuando se expresan en aislado para compensar el patrón prosódico de (2b).
new_statements.translation: The simple stems of Mazahua have a syllabic trochaic pattern, i.e. one strong syllable and one weak syllable (Knapp 2008: 95; Arellanes & Romero 2022: 2). [...] The first thing to consider is that the language is disyllabic of type (2b) [CV.CV] and always seeks to reflect that at all its levels (phonetic, morphological, syntactic). Second, stress and the distinctive tone fall on the first syllable of the simple (or compound) stem; the tone of the second syllable of the stem (the thematic formative) is fully predictable, see Table 4 below. Along these lines, monosyllabic lexemes of type (2a) [...] undergo phonetic rearticulation when uttered in isolation to compensate for the prosodic pattern of (2b).
new_statements.citation: Victoria Sebastián, Antonio. 2024. Interfaz sintáctico-semántica de los argumentos verbales en el mazahua de San Antonio de la Laguna. Tesis de doctorado en Lingüística Indoamericana, Centro de Investigaciones y Estudios Superiores en Antropología Social (CIESAS) / INPI, Ciudad de México.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File check: (474 pp., CIESAS handle 1015/1720; URL re-probed now, HTTP 200, 3,777,315 bytes = copies we hold). Sec. 2.2.3 'Inventario silábico y tonal': printed p. 44 (PDF 57) opens 'Los radicales simples de la lengua mazahua tienen un patrón trocaico silábico, es decir, una sílaba fuerte y otra sílaba débil (Knapp 2008: 95, Arellanes y Romero 2022: 2).'; printed p. 46 (PDF 59, confirmed with extracted text) has 'Lo primero a considerar es que la lengua es bisilábica del tipo (2b).. Segundo, el acento y el tono distintivo caen en la primera sílaba del radical simple (o compuesto), el tono de la segunda sílaba del radical (o formativo temático) es totalmente predecible, véase la Tabla 4 abaj…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the first syllable of the stem (radical), i.e. the root syllable, which also carries the one lexically distinctive tone (H, L, HL, LH); the following syllable (stem formative/suffix) is weak with predictable tone, giving a syllabic trochee. Proclitics (TAM/person markers) precede the stressed root syllable and are unstressed; monosyllabic roots are rearticulated (pa -> [ˈpa.ʔa]) in isolation to fill the trochaic template. Same rule as Knapp 2008: 95 for central Mazahua ('siempre se acentúa la primer sílaba del radical').
new_statements.secondary_stress: None described as such; the 2018 MA thesis (p. 18 n. 2) calls the root-syllable stress 'acento primario'. Clitic strings are said to group into additional trochaic feet (2024: sec. 2.3.3; Tlalocan 2025: 62, e.g. [ˌkʰa.ʔa] with a secondary mark on an existential), but no secondary-stress rule is formulated.
new_statements.exceptions: Compounds and Spanish loans do not follow the tonal pattern of simple stems (Tlalocan 2025: 61-62), though they are still transcribed with initial stress ([ˈpeɾ.so.na], [ˈsiɾ.βe]); stems of shape CVʔCˀV restrict tone contrasts to H/L; monosyllabic stems rearticulate in isolation.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the stem/phonological word: proclitics sit outside the foot, suffixes (object markers, stem formative) fill the weak syllable; statements are based on verbs in citation and in glossed texts (IPA lines in the Tlalocan texts mark stress on every phonological word). Language is tonal (4 tones) with stress explicitly described alongside tone.
new_statements.identity_note: All three sources with a stress statement (Victoria Sebastián 2018, 2024; Victoria Sebastián & Hernández Peña 2025) describe the Mazahua (jñatrjo) of San Antonio de la Laguna, municipio Donato Guerra, Estado de México, which the author classes as 'mazahua de occidente' (INALI 2008) = Western Mazahua; Glottolog 5.x files these SAL theses under mich1246 'Michoacán Mazahua' [mmc] (Moseley: 'Western Mazahua'), not under cent2144. The community is on the Estado de México side of the western dialect area, not in Michoacán. The one source from Michoacán proper (Mora-Bustos & Mora Muñoz 2016, Crescencio Morales, Zitácuaro) says only that the language is tonal with mainly disyllabic words. The rule found is identical to the one already catalogued for Central Mazahua cent2144 (Knapp 2008: 95 via Arellanes & Romero 2021), and Victoria explicitly adopts Knapp's formulation for SAL with his own data (tone tables, IPA-transcribed texts with stress marks).
